description: The coal railway of the Abbey Mills Pumping Station on the OS five-foot plan (1893): a fan of four sidings along the north-east side of the engine house, joining one lead that runs south-east along the foot of the Northern Outfall Sewer bank, passes under the Long Wall path ramp and turns south onto the Channelsea quay below the sewer bridge, where barges were unloaded. Drawn by docs/factory-yards.js as ground-level yard track on a cinder yard yardHalfWidthMetres either side (scripts/build_factory_yards.py, site 9101); the track bed is made ground (data/maps/made-ground.json, abbey-mills-coal-sidings).
source: OS London five-foot plan, 1893 (reference/nls-tiles os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18, scripts/factory_map_sources.py mosaic)
method: Each siding followed from its north-west end by a line follower on the plan's rail lines (1 m steps, re-centred on the dark lines within 0.9 m each step), smoothed over 7 m and simplified to 0.15 m. A branch ends where it meets the line it joins (within 0.9 m). The lead is the north-eastern siding continued to the quay join, then the quay track traced south from it. Positions are good to about a metre; switches and crossings are not drawn.

tracks.role: lead and north-eastern siding, to the Channelsea quay
siding, joins the lead near the tank
siding beside the engine house, joins siding 3

notTraced: The single heavy line north-east of the fan, along the foot of the sewer bank, is read as a fence or wall, not a siding.

The east-west water south of the station: closed at both ends on the 1893 plan (square at the west by the south building; short of the Long Wall bank at the east, with no lock, sluice or culvert lettered). Not a barge basin; probably a drain or pond. Not added.

unloading.place: The Channelsea quay below the sewer bridge, where the lead turns south along the west bank (the author's 'basin' for the coal, 6 October 2026).
unloading.tide: Unloading only near high water (author, from the photographs): the quay is below the tidal limit at Abbey Mill, so at low water the barges lay on the mud. The model's tide shows both states.
unloading.wallFace: The OS draws a continuous double line along the west bank from the sewer bridge south past the quay to about z 43. Added in task E, F3 as abbey-mills-coal-quay-wall in data/maps/os-river-walls.json, so it draws as a masonry quay wall.
